title: Lightweight Fusion & Adaptive Launch Strategies for Low-latency FlashAttention with Paged KV
body:
Purpose
This doc sketches an approach for a lightweight operator-fusion layer and an adaptive kernel-launch strategy targeted at low-latency streaming inference using FlashAttention-style attention kernels over models that use a paged KV cache. The goal is to reduce per-token latency and CPU/GPU synchronization overhead while preserving predictable latency SLOs for tail requests. It focuses on small to medium sequence lengths (1–1024) and workloads with heterogeneous sequence distributions (short user prompts followed by long generation).

Problem summary
- FlashAttention kernels are extremely fast for dense attention, but repeatedly launching multiple kernels (attention -> ff -> norm -> state update -> KV page management) increases host-device synchronization and kernel enqueue overhead for low-token workloads.
- Paged KV introduces asynchronous device memory residency changes; naive prefetch leads to stalls or overfetching.
- Existing heavy-weight fusion attempts (full graph fusion into a single kernel) increase code complexity, long compile times, and brittle fallback behavior. We need a middle ground that: 1) fuses hot operator pairs/triples (lightweight fusion), 2) keeps kernels small enough to reuse existing FlashAttention implementations, and 3) adapts launch configuration to current KV residency and request latency budget.

Design goals
- Minimize extra device-to-host round trips and CUDA stream stalls per token.
- Avoid monolithic kernels: keep reuse and maintainability high.
- Maintain deterministic memory footprint for paged KV and safe fallback when pages miss.
- Offer a runtime policy that chooses between fused vs unfused kernels and microbatching vs streaming.
- Make instrumentation cheap and fine-grained (per-token latency histogram, kernel enqueue times, KV page hit/miss counters).

Key concepts and components
1) Lightweight fusion tiles
- Define small fused primitives that combine adjacent compute-bound ops commonly used together: e.g., FlashAttention + Bias+Mask application; Attention(output) + AddResidual + LayerNormScaleUpdate; FlashAttention + KV-producer writeback (for autoregressive work).
- Each fused tile remains limited to a handful of operator stages (2–3) and exposes a narrow interface: inputs, masks, optional prefetch hints, and scalar flags for in-place/residual behaviors.
- Benefit: reduces scratch memory copies between kernels and removes host-side reconfiguration between ops.

2) Adaptive launch controller (ALC)
- A small runtime policy that decides kernel selection and launch config per-request or per-microbatch based on: latency_budget_ms, page_residency_estimate, recent_kernel_latency_p50/p95, current_queued_tokens.
- ALC keeps a tiny running window (100–1000 samples) of metrics and uses cost heuristics to choose: fused_tile vs base_kernels, block/grid sizing (occupancy vs latency tradeoff), and whether to prefetch pages synchronously or asynchronously.

3) Paged KV prefetch hints and soft-eviction
- Each request carries a compact prefetch_hint structure: list of KV-page-ids (small array, typically 1–4), priority (0..3), and deadline_ms.
- Lightweight prefetcher issues async page pulls to device pool; the ALC may delay kernel launch for a short backoff when misses are small and latency_budget permits; otherwise it switches to a compatible fallback model variant (smaller context or lower-precision) or runs unfused path that can stream data in chunks.
- Soft-eviction: when device memory pressure is high, prefer evicting least-likely pages (based on simple recency + stride heuristics) but keep 1–2 hot pages pinned per active stream.

4) Kernel API and handshake
- Kernels accept a compact header in device-visible pinned memory with fields: op_flags, sequence_len, kv_page_bitmap (bitmask for small caches), prefetch_token_id, out_ptr, scratch_ptr, policy_version.
- Host writes header then enqueues kernel asynchronously; kernel reads header to know whether all pages are guaranteed resident or whether it should switch to a streaming subpath.
- Streaming subpath: if a critical KV page is missing, kernel falls back to processing available prefix and emits a device->host notification to continue once page arrives. This avoids device waiting on host CPU.

Scheduling heuristics and launch strategies
- Latency-first small tokens: prefer fused tiles with low occupancy (more SMs per CTA, smaller blocks) to reduce queueing latency. Use warp-occupancy tuning to minimize head-of-line delay.
- Throughput-first large batches: use unfused, high-occupancy launches with larger blocks that maximize FLOPS and memory bandwidth.
- KV-miss-aware path: if predicted page miss probability > threshold, prefer unfused streaming path that processes available prefix and overlaps prefetch with compute.

Memory layout and alignment considerations
- Align KV page allocations to 256KB multiples to simplify page mapping and avoid straddling. This makes bitmap checks cheap and reduces bank conflicts for commonly accessed head-of-sequence areas.
- Adopt blocked KV slab layout: contiguous per-key blocks matching flashattention tile widths (e.g., 128/256) to improve coalescing during readback and reduce per-access latency.

Instrumentation and metrics to collect
- Per-kernel enqueue -> start -> end timestamps to compute host enqueue latency vs device runtime.
- KV page hit/miss counters with latency distribution for each page id (store in a ring buffer for recent N accesses).
- Policy decisions logged at high level: reason_for_choice (latency_budget|page_miss|high_load), selected_kernel_variant, predicted_vs_actual_latency.
- Export lightweight histograms (p50,p90,p99) and the distribution of fused vs unfused usage.

Micro-batching vs streaming tradeoffs
- Micro-batching reduces per-token overhead but increases tail latency for the first token in a batch. ALC will use a simple formula:
  effective_latency = queuing_delay + per_token_latency/microbatch_size
  choose microbatch_size that minimizes effective_latency under throughput constraints.
- For autoregressive workloads with strong tail-SLO requirements, default microbatch_size=1 for interactive tier; allow up to 8 for bulk generation.

Experiment plan (short-term)
- Implement a prototype ALC with two fused tiles: (1) FlashAttention + BiasMask, (2) Attention out + ResidualAdd.
- Add KV prefetch hint plumbing through SDK to propagate small page-id arrays.
- Run synthetic workloads: short-prompt (avg seq 16, gen 64), mixed (16/256), and long (1024) under 99th percentile latency SLO target 150ms.
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 token latency, GPU utilization, host enqueue time, page-miss rate, and cost (tokens/sec per GPU).

Open questions / risks
- Complexity of maintaining multiple kernel variants and ensuring correctness across fp16/int8 quantized paths.
- Hardware variability: tuned block sizes on one GPU (A100) may be poor on another (H100); need lightweight device profiles.
- Interaction with CUDA multi-stream scheduling and other tenants on shared GPUs. Might need stricter device isolation for latency tier.

Next steps
- (Short) Build a minimal fused-kernel wrapper that calls existing FlashAttention code path and avoids extra memcpy for bias/mask.
- (Near) Implement ALC heuristics and metric collectors; expose a debug mode to force variants.
- (Med) Extend prefetch hint SDK and integrate with KV manager; add page residency estimator.
- (Long) Add automated tuner that recommends fused vs unfused thresholds per model and per device family.

Appendix: simple ALC decision pseudocode
  decide_kernel(request):
    budget = request.latency_budget_ms
    page_hit_prob = kv_estimator.probability_all_pages_resident(request.prefetch_hint)
    if budget < LOW_LATENCY_THRESHOLD:
      if page_hit_prob > 0.95:
        return fused_tile_low_occupancy
      else:
        return streaming_unfused
    else:
      if request.seq_len > LARGE_SEQ_THRESHOLD:
        return unfused_high_occupancy
      else:
        return fused_tile_balanced

Notes to reviewers: this is a working sketch intended to start engineering experiments — not a finalized API. Feedback especially welcome on the header handshake approach and minimal prefetch hint shape.
